BiblicalUsage: Kanash is to assemble — to gather together, here the gathering of the whole empire before Nebuchadnezzar's image. The princes, the governors, the captains, the judges, the treasurers, the counsellors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces were gathered together unto the dedication of the image; and after the furnace, the same princes gathered together and saw that the fire had no power upon the bodies of the three.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two gatherings frame the story: the empire assembles to worship an image, and then assembles again to see that the fire could not touch the faithful. God gathers His witnesses too, and His gathering is the one that lasts.
